claims.text: Combining thermodynamic integration or metadynamics with machine-learning interatomic potentials can compute solid-liquid free-energy differences in high-entropy alloys accurately and efficiently.
The relative Gibbs free energies of competing phases determine phase stability.
Enhanced solid-liquid free-energy sampling incorporates atomic interactions and entropy contributions.
The proposed calculations will directly yield melting temperatures.
The proposed calculations will directly yield enthalpies and entropies of fusion.
The proposed calculations will directly yield volume changes at melting and liquid-phase thermodynamic properties with quantified errors.
The approach is applicable to fcc-, bcc-, and hcp-structured high-entropy alloys near melting.
Configurational and thermal contributions are important to the near-melting thermodynamics of these alloys.
Machine-learning interatomic potentials can accurately capture both configurational disorder and thermal vibrational properties in high-entropy alloys.
Machine learning improves potential accuracy across the vast multicomponent composition space.
Thermodynamic integration or metadynamics provides latent heats and volume changes with statistical error bars.
The framework will predict melting and fusion properties within approximately 10–20% of experiment.
Agreement within 10–20% across diverse high-entropy-alloy compositions would validate the approach across the family.
The approach applies from ambient to moderate pressures across a wide range of multicomponent compositions.
Existing CALPHAD methods lack efficiency over the high-entropy-alloy composition space.
First-principles approaches are difficult or expensive to apply across very large alloy spaces.
Existing CALPHAD and ab initio approaches do not provide comprehensive error quantification for the proposed outputs.
Applicability is restricted to systems for which reliable machine-learning interatomic potentials can be developed.
Significant electronic-structure changes can reduce the effectiveness of the proposed framework.
Failure of a potential to capture short-range order can reduce the effectiveness of the proposed framework.
